directions.hypothesis: Baltimore is down to its third quarterback, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. He went 10 of 21 for 91 yards with an interception in his debut and is now hurt. Jacksonville has covered often as a favorite. Several outlets say Jaguars by double digits, but that counts as one lead. The line moved from -7.5 to about -10, so much of the edge may already be in the price. Kickoff is Thu Nov 5, 8:15 PM EST.
directions.question: Is the line now past -9.5, Covers' stated playable limit? And does Fagnano's knee/ankle injury mean an even less experienced QB starts, already reflected in the spread?

directions.hypothesis: This is the contrarian view from VSiN. It argues more than a touchdown is too many points for a home team that can lean on Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews. Jacksonville's defensive line is also thinner, with DaVon Hamilton out and Travon Walker dealing with a rib injury. If the game is a slow, run-heavy grind, a double-digit cushion could hold. The same writer also put a small bet on the Ravens moneyline at +410.
directions.question: Can Baltimore protect the ball with Fagnano? Jacksonville's defense creates a lot of turnovers and short fields. Also, is +10.5 still available, and at what price?

directions.hypothesis: The Under case: Baltimore has scored 13 or fewer in three straight games, its QB is a hurt third-stringer, and Jacksonville allows the second-fewest points in the league. Covers' Osborne also leaned Under 42.5, which is the same take. The skeptical view is that the total has already dropped from 48.5 to 39.5, so the obvious Under may be priced in.
directions.question: Has the total settled near 39.5 or lower? Could Jacksonville get close to it alone? It scored 73 points in its last two games and Baltimore allowed 71 in its last two.

directions.hypothesis: With both top QBs out, running Henry a lot is Baltimore's most likely game plan. VSiN called this a lean, not a bet, noting Henry hasn't had an 18-carry game in three games. The real risk is falling far behind early, which would cut his carries.
directions.question: If Jacksonville leads by two scores by halftime, does Baltimore's coaching staff abandon the run? And has the carries line moved above 17.5?

directions.hypothesis: Jacksonville's run defense may be weakening. It allowed 63.8 rushing yards per game over its first five games, then 100+ in each of the last two, and is now missing DaVon Hamilton with Travon Walker banged up. Henry has historically done well against Jacksonville. But stacked boxes against a weak passing game could limit his yards per carry even if he gets a lot of carries.
directions.question: Will Jacksonville crowd the line of scrimmage because Fagnano can't make them pay through the air? Also, is Henry's yardage line already raised because of his history against the Jaguars?

directions.hypothesis: Fagnano is an undrafted rookie who threw for 91 yards on 21 attempts in his debut. He is playing hurt on a short week against a top scoring defense, and Baltimore is expected to run heavily. Two things could hurt an Under: the line may already be very low, and if Baltimore falls behind it may have to throw a lot of garbage-time passes.
directions.question: Is Fagnano confirmed as the starter? Reports differ on whether his injury is to the knee or ankle, and one says even his start isn't guaranteed. Also, how low is his passing-yards line?

directions.hypothesis: Tuten is coming off a career-high 104 rushing yards and has at least 87 scrimmage yards in all but one game. If Jacksonville builds a lead, it should run often against a Baltimore defense that has allowed a lot of running back touchdowns.
directions.question: How are carries split among Jacksonville's backs, especially late in a blowout? And has his rushing line already jumped after the career game?

directions.hypothesis: Covers' published pick is a Strange anytime touchdown, which isn't one of our markets, so this direction asks whether his target volume carries over to receptions. He has seen seven or more targets in three of his last four games, and Baltimore has allowed six touchdowns to tight ends. The main risk is that Jacksonville barely throws if it controls the game: Trevor Lawrence completed only 10 passes in Week 8.
directions.question: If Jacksonville leads early, will Lawrence throw enough for Strange to clear his receptions line, or will they run out the clock?
